Remote Enantioselective ɛ-Alkylation of Copper
Ethynylallenylidenes: Precise Control of Central and Axial Chirality
Yu-Hua Wen, Minghao Liu, Yu-Hao Wang, Qian-Wei Gong, Shuai Li, Jin Song,* and
Liu-Zhu Gong*
Abstract: Chiral tetrasubstituted allenes have emerged
as important architectures for engineering biologically
active compounds. The construction of unique tetrasub-
stituted allene scaffolds with precise control of continu-
ous central and axial chirality remains yet to be
developed. Here, we report a remote enantioselective ɛ-
alkylation of yne-propargylic acetates with enals enabled
by NHC and copper cooperative catalysis, leading to a
series of tetrasubstituted allenes with excellent enantio-
selectivities (up to > 99 % ee) and diastereoselectivities
(up to >95 :5 dr). This method features high regioselec-
tivity and simultaneous control of axial and central
chirality. Mechanistic studies suggest a cooperative
activation mode and synergistic control of distal chirality
created from the copper ethynylallenylidenes.

Introduction

tivity patterns. They have frequently been utilized as
fundamental components in various downstream transfor-
mations and have also functioned as important elements in
bioactive natural products, functional materials, and asym-

stantial efforts have been devoted to the construction of
axially chiral allenes.<sup>[2]</sup> Nevertheless, the development of
feasible synthetic methods to access optically active fully
substituted allenes poses particular challenges.<sup>[3]</sup> Since the
pioneering research conducted by Ma,<sup>[4]</sup> Sun,<sup>[5]</sup> and co-
workers, regio- and stereoselective functionalization of
propargyl alcohols containing internal alkyne groups has
been achieved through metal catalysis<sup>[6]</sup> and

efficient transformations to access fully substituted chiral
allenes. Nevertheless, new concepts enabling catalytic asym-
metric synthesis of chiral allenes bearing vicinal stereo-
centers, especially those densely functionalized, remains
rather rare.<sup>[8]</sup> The fundamental obstacle to address this issue
is the lack of a reliable stereocontrol model that allows the
tetrasubstituted allenes to be accessed by asymmetric
catalysis in a highly stereoselective manner.

Remote stereocontrol is a pivotal concept in the field of
organic synthesis, referring to the ability to manipulate the
stereochemistry of a molecule through the influence of
functional groups located at a distance, and has long been a
challenging and highly interesting focus in the field of
asymmetric catalysis.<sup>[9]</sup> Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmet-
ric substitution of propargylic alcohol derivatives serves as
one of the most powerful and reliable methods for
constructing carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bonds
with propargylic stereocenters.<sup>[10]</sup> Recently, the groups of
Xu,<sup>[11]</sup> He,<sup>[12]</sup> Lin,<sup>[13]</sup> Fang,<sup>[14]</sup> and Huang<sup>[15]</sup> conquered the
obstacle of regio- and stereoselectivity at more than three
bonds distance from the metal center in the stereoselective
coupling events of copper-bound electrophiles with amines,
1,3-dicarbonyl compounds, sodium sulfinates, and arene
nucleophiles. While these examples of asymmetric remote
functionalization are pioneering, they are limited to the
synthesis of chiral yne-allylic derivatives. Yne-propargylic
acetates with a terminal alkyne group, featuring easy
availability, represent a new type of highly functionalized
molecules and hold significant potential in organic synthesis;
however, they have not yet received enough attention.
Principally, they can undergo carbocupration to form copper
ethynylallenylidenes that might be able to undergo an
asymmetric remote ɛ-alkylation reaction to access chiral
tetrasubstituted allenes or a classical propargylation process
at γ-carbon (Figure 1c).

N-Heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-mediated umpolung re-
activity has paved the way to numerous significant
reactions.<sup>[16]</sup> NHC/transition metal cooperative catalysis<sup>[17]</sup>
has showcased its robustness by enabling new transforma-
tions that surpass the capabilities of individual catalytic
systems.<sup>[18]</sup> Within this context, our group discovered that
the NHC-bound isatin-derived homoenolate equivalents<sup>[19]</sup>
showed high reactivity toward a broad range of transition
metal-activated electrophilic species, culminating in diverse
protocols to access a wide spectrum of chiral oxindole
derivatives bearing tetrasubstituted stereocenters with re-
markable efficiency and stereoselectivity.<sup>[20]</sup> As a conse-

homoenolates might be sufficiently reactive to undergo the

γ-carbon appearing to be even more (see preliminary DFT
calculations in Supporting Information), thus the identifica-
tion of optimal NHC and copper dual catalyst capable of
leveraging the regioselectivity comes foremost. In addition,
remote control of the stereoselectivity is always highly
challenging. In this case, the ɛ-carbon locates five carbons
away from the copper bonded to the chiral ligand and is part
of a linear π-system, which further complicates the stereo-
selective creation of axial chirality. Moreover, the simulta-
neous control of both axial and central chirality would be
another key element for the realization of the proposed
reaction. Herein, we report NHC/Cu cooperatively catalyzed

derived enals and yne-propargylic acetates with precise
control of the regio- and enantioselectivity of both central
and axial chirality.
Results and Discussion
We began our investigation into the asymmetric allenylation
reaction of yne-propargylic acetate 1a and enal 2a in the
presence of 3 mol% of copper salt, 6 mol% of Pybox ligand
L1, and 20 mol% of NHC precatalyst 4a in tetrahydrofuran at
25°C (Table 1). To our delight, the reaction preferred the ɛ-
alkylation reaction over the γ-propargylation, leading to chiral
tetrasubstituted allene 3aa in high yield and with great
stereoselectivity, together with a trace amount of γ-regiomer of
the alkylation product 3aa’ (Table 1, entry 1, and also see
Table S1 in the Supporting Information for details). Ligand
screening revealed that L1 was the most competent one for the
copper catalyst to achieve the highest enantioselectivity
(entry 1 vs 2–5). Evaluation of chiral NHC precatalysts showed
that using 20 mol% of precatalyst 4d allowed 3aa to be
isolated in an acceptable 42% yield and with excellent
stereoselectivity (93:7 dr, 99% ee, entry 8 vs 6–9). Survey of
solvents, including dichloromethane, 1,4-dioxane, and toluene,
suggested that THF turned out to be the most suitable reaction
media in terms of reaction conversion and stereoselectivity
(entry 8 vs 10–12). Lowering the reaction temperature could
further enhance both the yield and stereoselectivity, and the
desired allene-oxindole 3aa was successfully obtained in 73%
yield with 95:5 dr and 99% ee (entry 13).
Using the optimized reaction conditions (Table 1, en-
try 13), we then explored the generality of the NHC/Cu
cooperatively catalyzed ɛ-alkylation reaction. First, the
scope of yne-propargylic acetates 1 was examined
(Scheme 1, top). Substrates bearing an electron-donating or
-withdrawing substituent at the para position of the benzene
ring were tolerated, furnishing the corresponding products
(3 ba–3ha) in good yields and excellent stereoselectivities
(up to > 95 : 5 dr, 99 % ee). Yne-propargylic acetates
incorporating either a methyl or a methoxy substituent at
the meta-position proved to be good substrates. As show-
cased by examples 3ka and 3la, yne-propargylic acetates 2
bearing 2-fluorophenyl and 3,4-dimethoxyphenyl were also
accommodated. The reaction of 3-methyl-1-(naphthalen-2-
yl)penta-1,4-diyn-3-yl acetate (1 b) with enal 2 a successfully
delivered 3ma in 50% yield with 94 : 6 dr and 99 % ee.
Moreover, yne-propargylic acetates with either linear or
branched alkyl substituents at the γ-carbon also participated
in the reaction smoothly, as exemplified by 3na–3ra which
were generated in 95–99 % ee. We next carried out reactions
of propargylic acetates bearing methyl and butyl-substituted
alkyne moieties. The desired alkylation products 3sa and
3ta could be obtained in high yields and enantioselectivities,
but the diastereoselectivity was rather poor. Unfortunately,
the desired product 3ua was not isolated when the R<sup>1</sup> group
is tert-butyl. Furthermore, the absolute configuration of 3aa
was assigned by single-crystal X-ray analysis.<sup>[21]</sup> Next, we
explored the scope of isatin-derived α,β-unsaturated alde-
hydes 2 (Scheme 1, bottom). The N-substituent, including
Et, Bn, and allyl groups, did not show considerable effect on
the reaction performance, giving rise to the target ɛ-
alkylation adducts (3 ab–3ad) in good yields (54–65 %) and
with excellent stereoselectivities (92 : 8 dr, 93–96 % ee).

As shown in Figure 3a, to even better understand the
mechanism, some related kinetic experiments were per-
formed under the standard conditions and the initial rates of
the reaction were measured. The NHC/Cu cooperatively
catalyzed reaction appeared to have a first-order depend-
ence on the concentrations of the copper catalyst, NHC
precatalyst 4d, yne-propargylic acetate 1a, and enal 2 a as
well. The first-order dependence on both the catalysts and
substrates indicates that each plays a role in the rate-limiting
steps. Based on these results, we proposed a catalytic
reaction cycle shown in Figure 3b. The NHC catalyst 4d
reacts with the enal 2a and delivers the Breslow intermedi-
ate I (azolium homoenolate species II). The coordination of
the chiral copper catalyst to the yne-propargylic acetate 1a,
followed by a deprotonation process, affords an alkyne
copper intermediate III. The subsequent elimination of an
acetyl group delivers a copper ethynylallenylidene complex
V (resonant intermediate IV). Then, the above two inter-
mediates (II and V) approach each other, and the chiral
NHC catalyst along with the copper complex works cooper-
atively during the intermolecular asymmetric remote alle-
nylic alkylation process to yield an adduct VI. Finally, the
alcoholysis of the intermediate VI with methanol leads to
the oxindole-containing tetrasubstituted allene 3aa.
Conclusion
In summary, we have demonstrated that the combination of a
chiral copper complex and a chiral N-heterocyclic carbene
effectively catalyzes the asymmetric allenylic alkylation reac-
tion of isatin-derived enals with yne-propargylic acetates. This
method allows the remote ɛ-alkylation of copper ethynylalle-
nylidenes to couple with NHC-bound nucleophiles and to give
tetrasubstituted allene scaffolds with precise control of con-
tinuous central and axial chirality (up to >95:5 dr, >99% ee).
Mechanistic investigations have revealed that the cooperative
activation mode as well as the matched chirality of the ligand
and NHC exerts considerable impact on both reaction
efficiency and stereoselectivity. We anticipate that this study
will inspire further exploration of cooperative organo- and
copper-catalyzed remote activation reactions.
